liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Truckin'** (5 reviews): The second set's Truckin' jam is excellent; Truckin' leads into a jam called the 'Wood Green Jam', then Wharf Rat; these appear on Dick's Picks 7 [7][8][10][11][16]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (3 reviews): Scarlet Begonias, Mexicali Blues and Row Jimmy from this show appear on Dick's Picks 7; Scarlet Begonias, on Dick's Picks 7, is judged nothing special [8][10][16]
- **Playin' In The Band** (2 reviews): Version reaches the magical early-seventies quality, though Donna is not at her best; Playin' is now available, having been missing from the Dick's Picks release [7][14]

## The recordings

- **gd1974-09-09.135655.sbd.new.patched.miller.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 146 min; rated 2/5 by 3 [1]. Said about its sound: Upgrade over the same tracks on Dick's Picks 7, with extra tracks of equal quality [14]
- **gd1974-09-09.154544.aud.flegel.flac1644**: audience recording; 19 songs; 153 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd74-09-09.sbd.sly.12846.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 115 min; rated 2.57/5 by 7 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the show sounds good [13]
- **gd1974-09-09.sbd.dp7-outtakes.sirmick.fix-32642.97013.flac16**: soundboard; 10 songs; 62 min; rated 1.67/5 by 3 [4]. Said about its sound: Soundcheck Jack Straw cleaned of static and EQ'd because it sounded lifeless; pops removed in Promised Land [4]
- **gd1974-09-09.sbd.dp7-outtakes.sirmick.32642.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 10 songs; 61 min [5]. Said about its sound: Static reduced at start of soundcheck Jack Straw, EQ'd, pops removed in Promised Land, Deal-El Paso transition cleaned [5]

## Around the show

- Weir apologizes to the audience at least twice for the late start [10]
- First London/Europe show in over two years; tour was just four cities, opening with three nights at Ally Pally, built in 1875 [17]
- A sound system was shipped over, but the full Wall of Sound was not feasible [17]
- The band played one long set, slotted after Traffic [17]
- First London/Europe show in over two years; tour was just four cities, opening with three nights at Ally Pally, built in 1875 [18]
- A sound system was shipped over, but the full Wall of Sound was not feasible [18]
- The band played one long set, slotted after Traffic [18]
- Uploader wonders whether the Jack Straw is a soundcheck; Uncle John's Band follows Wharf Rat and One More Saturday Night is a second encore [1]
- Good precursor to the two stronger shows at the same venue that followed [7]
- Considered the least interesting music on Dick's Picks 7 and far from the year's best [11]
- Called one of the dullest shows of 1974 [12]
- Dick's Picks 7 cut other jams, including those in Truckin' and Playin'; the show itself sounds good [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1974-09-09.135655.sbd.new.patched.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat [1]. Also: Patch source is rough but the only one the uploader could find [1]
- **gd1974-09-09.154544.aud.flegel.flac1644**: taped by Unkown; transferred by Brian Flegel; source: Unknown [2]. Also: Cassette audience source burned to CD via a ~1989 TC-WE475 cassette deck and ~2001 Sony burner; Row Jimmy, Uncle John's Band and Johnny B. Goode patched from Charlie Miller's soundboard source, with crossfading and volume adjustment [2]
- **gd74-09-09.sbd.sly.12846.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]
- **gd1974-09-09.sbd.dp7-outtakes.sirmick.fix-32642.97013.flac16**: transferred by SIRMick; source: sbd > mr > dat (x2) > cdr [4]. Also: Fix of an earlier transfer: repeated Playin' section removed and replaced by Deal, with tracks taken from shnid 12846 [4]
- **gd1974-09-09.sbd.dp7-outtakes.sirmick.32642.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by SirMick; source: sbd > mr > dat (x2) > cdr > eac > mkwact > wav > flac [5]. Also: Tracks taken from shnid 12846; Playin' originally split in three parts was rejoined; all appear on Dick's Picks Volume 7 [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Alexandra Palace - September 9, 1974](https://www.dead.net/show/september-9-1974) [21]
